title: Securing Grandma's groceries with Pierre Cadieux
content_md: This month, Amy is joined by Pierre Cadieux, Research Lead for Intelligence Efficacy at Talos. Pierre takes us back to his early days on help desks in the 90s, where learning to correlate logs between Windows and Unix systems sparked the curiosity that eventually led him to security. It’s a great look at how someone who has seen the industry evolve over decades stays grounded and keeps their edge. We also get into what’s kept Pierre at Cisco for nearly ten years. He talks about why he prioritizes the human impact of our work, the importance of knowing when to step away from the keyboard, and how his background in anthropology actually informs the way he approaches threat intelligence today. Amy Ciminnisi: I've known you since you were in Talos IR, which was not too long ago. But tell me a little bit about your professional journey, because I know that definitely was not the start of it. Pierre Cadieux: I worked at an ISP as part of the help desk back in the mid-90s. I was one of the people who people would call up and say, "Hey, I've got this computer I just bought, how do I get it on the internet?" I did a lot of learning about what TCP/IP was, what networking was, how to connect things via various different types of connections — whether it be an actual hard-coded network connection or a dial-up connection — and was able to get some expertise around guiding people through that process.
